script.base: Close dome game, not a blowout: LAC -3.5, implied LAC 25.0 / LV 21.5 on 46.5. LAC leads by about a score late but both QBs keep throwing. LV's week-1 run wall (3.33 YPC, one 10+ run) can stall Omarion Hampton (15/48) and lean Justin Herbert toward Keenan Allen (10 targets), Ladd McConkey (9) and Quentin Johnston (7). Ashton Jeanty keeps a full carry share in a one-score game rather than a pure chase. Pace is normal, pass-lean, full starter snaps.
script.flip1: LAC gets up by 14+ early, kills clock with Hampton, and Herbert/Allen/McConkey/Johnston yards stall after the lead (same shape as a favorite finishing with a quiet passing box). LV abandons the run, so Jeanty's 19-carry role dies and Meyers/Bowers/Thornton targets spike.
script.flip2: LV hangs around or leads. Geno Smith, who posted 0.57 EPA/dropback vs blitz vs 0.26 clean, and Jakobi Meyers/Brock Bowers/Dont'e Thornton push pace up. Jeanty stays on the field, LAC has to throw, and Allen/McConkey air yards convert together in a mini-shootout.

No LAC skill player is out, so Allen/McConkey/Johnston/Hampton roles are unchanged from week 1.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. LAC led by two scores at half, LV went pass-only behind a line missing Jackson Powers-Johnson, and Jeanty finished around 11 carries and 30 yards, under 38.5, because the dog-abandon flip beat a one-game 5.76 YPC sample and a Perryman absence that Phillips or Henley may have covered. Allen stalled in the 50s because Las Vegas' real profile was the outside (right 5.28 YPA on 18 throws, only 50 yards on three 20+ balls), the 8.57 middle mark was seven throws of noise, and McConkey or Johnston took the intermediate work. The counter-case is about as strong as the read: n=1 both ways, lines a half-yard off the only box score, no chart, no price. It is not clearly stronger, so the leans stay flagged rather than promoted or silently cut.
